newsitem.title: GERMANY: Full non-EMU bank TARGET access a problem-Buba.
newsitem.headline: Full non-EMU bank TARGET access a problem-Buba.

text.p: The Bundesbank on Tuesday warned that full participation in the TARGET payments system by central banks which were not part of Europe's single currency could hurt the monetary policy of the European central Bank.

The German central bank also warned that giving equal terms to central banks outside European monetary union -- apart from giving unprecedented access to money creation in a foreign currency -- could disadvantage central banks within EMU.

Although there was general agreement that non-EMU banks could gain access to intraday credits in TARGET, is would be extremely difficult to prevent these drifting over into more damaging overnight credits, the bank said in a monthly report.
TARGET -- the acronym for Trans-European Automated Real-time Gross settlement Express Transfer system -- is the system which will ensure smooth transactions within the single currency area.

Britain in particular has argued that it ought to be given full access to this system even if it does not participate in the single currency, arguing that its financial centre London could be placed at an unfair disadvantage if this was denied.
Without mentioning Britain by name, the Bundesbank argued that full access to the system would not be appropriate in such a case.
"Even the extension of intraday credits to 'Out' central banks would set a precedent," the Bundesbank said. "No central bank so far allows others to take part in the creation of its own currency."

"The extension of credit to the central bank of a country which remains outside the currency union would disturb the monetary policy of the European central bank -- even if the volume and length of the credits remained limited," it added.
"Any form of credit extension increases liquidity, influences conditions on capital markets and is therefore relevant for monetary policy."
